To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the vertical acceleration response of footbridge is enhanced by crowd loading and this enhancement is a function of crowd density and synchronization.

(1) the vertical acceleration response of footbridge subjected to stochastic crowd is predicted by a probabilistic approach using statistical distribution of pedestrian parameters; (2) the vertical acceleration enhancement factors of footbridges due to crowd loading are proposed and verified by comparing the response of crowd loading with that of a single pedestrian; and (3) the enhancement factors for the vertical acceleration response due to crowd loading can be used to predict the vertical response of a footbridge subjected to crowd loading.

the vertical acceleration response of the bridge is enhanced by the crowd, the enhancement factor depends on the crowd density and the synchronization level, and the response is more sensitive to the crowd density than to the synchronization level.

the development of a probabilistic approach to predict vertical acceleration response of footbrides subjected to a crowd of pedestrians.
developing an enhanced understanding of the dynamic response of footbridge structures to pedestrian loading.
the vertical response of a footbridge to a stochastic crowd load.

the vertical response of a footbridge subjected to crowd loading can be predicted using the vertical response of an individual pedestrian, and that this response can be enhanced by a factor which is dependent on crowd density and synchronization level.

enhancement factors for the vertical acceleration response of footbridge structures subjected to stochastic crowd loads should be used in the design of footbridges to account for the effects of synchronization.
enhancement factors for vertical acceleration response of footbridge due to stochastic crowd loading is a function of the crowd density and synchronization level.

the vertical acceleration response of footbridge subjected to crowd loading can be predicted with a high degree of accuracy using the proposed probabilistic approach.

the vertical response of the footbridge due to crowd loading is not a simple linear combination of individual pedestrian loads and that enhancement factors are required to predict the vertical response of a footbridge due to a crowd of pedestrians.
a probabilistic approach can be used to predict vertical accelerations of a footbridge due to a crowd.

the response of footbrides due to crowd loading is significantly different to that due to single pedestrians.
the vertical response of a footbridge due to a crowd is more severe than due to a single pedestrian, and that this response can be predicted using a simple enhancement factor.
